selected_evidence.requirement: Existing inventory data is owned by inventorysvc
selected_evidence.summary: The complete tree is owned by `inventorysvc:inventory-readers`, both before and after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Inventory data is readable by inventory-readers and inaccessible to other users
selected_evidence.summary: Direct UID/GID tests show group-only read/traverse succeeds without write access, while an unrelated identity has no read, write, or traverse access.
The original `config.json` and `records.csv` remain present. Their pre-restart and post-restart checksums and sizes are identical.

selected_evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel were preserved

selected_evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID `76c76c44-3481-45c5-9707-6ff083e181eb`; restart was acknowledged; the recovered node reported changed boot ID `13616de0-2bf0-4a6e-9d7a-6d479ff4805e`; post-restart data, identities, permissions, and effective access all passed.

commands.command:
set -e
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf '%s\n' 'data_checksums_and_sizes:'
cksum /srv/inventory/data/config.json /srv/inventory/data/records.csv
printf '%s\n' 'tree_meta:'
find /srv/inventory -xdev -printf '%y %M %u:%g %s %p\n' | sort
python - <<'PY'
import os, pwd, grp, sys
root='/srv/inventory'
dirs=[root, root+'/data']
files=[root+'/data/config.json', root+'/data/records.csv']
svc=pwd.getpwnam('inventorysvc')
readers=grp.getgrnam('inventory-readers')
other=pwd.getpwnam('nobody')
cases=[
 ('owner', svc.pw_uid, readers.gr_gid, [readers.gr_gid], True, True, True),
 ('group_only', other.pw_uid, readers.gr_gid, [readers.gr_gid], True, False, True),
 ('other', other.pw_uid, other.pw_gid, [], False, False, False),
]
failed=False
for label,uid,gid,groups,expect_read,expect_write,expect_traverse in cases:
    pid=os.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.setgroups(groups)
        os.setgid(gid)
        os.setuid(uid)
        traversable=all(os.access(p, os.X_OK) for p in dirs)
        readable=all(os.access(p, os.R_OK) for p in files)
        writable=all(os.access(p, os.W_OK) for p in files)
        actual=(readable,writable,traversable)
        expected=(expect_read,expect_write,expect_traverse)
        print('%s uid=%d gid=%d read=%s write=%s traverse=%s expected=%s' % (label,uid,gid,readable,writable,traversable,actual==expected))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        os._exit(0 if actual==expected else 1)
    else:
        status=os.waitpid(pid,0)[1]
        if status != 0:
            failed=True
if failed:
    sys.exit(1)
PY
